content:
Implemented lane-level reordering across the workspace.

- Added a dedicated draggable lane-header handle with a lane-sized dashed placeholder, drag-state cleanup, and Up/Down keyboard reordering.
- Kept lane and tab drag state separate so tab reordering, cross-lane tab moves, and the new-group drop zone retain their existing behavior.
- Persisted `laneOrder` in shared `chrome.storage.local`, restored it during render, preserved temporarily hidden lanes, and rerendered every open window on storage changes.
- Mirrored all runtime changes into `meridian-extension/`.
- Added focused coverage for mouse/drop behavior, keyboard behavior, persistence ordering, hidden lanes, cross-window rerenders, and tab-drag isolation.

Verification:
- `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`: 165 passed, 0 failed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Source/package parity checks: passed.
- Headless Chrome DOM smoke: draggable handles rendered with accessible labels; ArrowDown reordered and retained focus; mouse drag activated the placeholder, committed lane order, and cleaned up drag state.

User rejection: dragging tabs or groups does not work in actual use, and the dedicated grab handles are unwanted. Rework so the group name itself is the drag target; verify real browser behavior rather than only fake-DOM tests.

Reworked after user rejection. Root cause was a real null-placeholder crash when dragging the last tab/lane (null compared equal to an uncreated placeholder, followed by null.nextElementSibling); fixed for both tab and lane paths. Removed grab handles entirely: the group name is now the draggable target. Full-card directional tab drops and full-target directional lane drops avoid the prior half-card/half-header dead zones. Verified lane-name dragging and persisted order in a real unpacked Chromium extension; full suite 170/170 passes.
Follow-up tweaks: keep an empty Unsorted lane available as a tab drop target, and fix single-click group-name rename so it selects only the title rather than all page text.

Applied the two requested follow-ups. Unsorted now renders even when empty, so it is always available as a drop target; dropping a grouped tab there calls the existing ungroup/unassign path. Rename selection now uses a Range scoped to the title instead of document.execCommand(selectAll), preventing page-wide selection. Real Chromium verification: empty Unsorted rendered with zero cards, dropping a grouped tab moved it there with groupId -1, and clicking the group name selected only that title. Full suite remains 170/170 green; focused tests 18/18 and source/package parity pass.
Correction from user: do not leave an empty Unsorted lane visible. Keep it hidden at rest and expose it only as a temporary drop target while a tab drag is active.

Corrected the empty-Unsorted behavior: the empty lane remains in the DOM as a valid drop target but is display:none at rest, becomes visible only while a local or cross-window tab drag is active, and hides again on drop/dragend (with timeout cleanup when an external drag leaves). Real Chromium check confirmed display none -> block during drag -> none after drag. Full suite 171/171 passes; parity and diff checks pass.
Regression: user reports all tab dragging is now broken after the transient empty-Unsorted change. Investigating native drag behavior and removing any layout shift at dragstart.

Fixed the tab-drag regression. Cause: revealing the hidden empty Unsorted lane at the top of the workspace during dragstart shifted the source card out from under the active pointer, disrupting native dragging. Empty Unsorted is now forced to the end of the workspace while empty, so revealing it adds only a bottom drop target and does not move any existing tab/group. Real Chromium DOM/Chrome-API verification confirmed the dragged card rect stays identical across dragstart and same-group tab reorder completes in the actual tab strip. Full suite 171/171 passes; parity/diff checks pass.
